sentences.text: Hello, and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
I am happy you are here.
Today, we will talk about Fiji.
Fiji is a group of islands in the Pacific Ocean.
Let's learn about it in simple English.
I will speak slowly.
You can listen and repeat if you want.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Fiji?
Fiji is in the South Pacific Ocean.
It is far from big continents.
It is close to New Zealand, Australia and Tonga.
Fiji is made of over 300 islands.
Only about 100 islands have people living on them.
What is the capital city of Fiji?
The capital city is Suva.
Suva is on the island of Vidi Livu.
It is the biggest city in Fiji.
It has shops, schools and offices.
Another big town is Nadi.
Nadi has the main airport.
Many tourists arrive there.
How many people live in Fiji?
About 900,000 people live in Fiji.
Most people live on the two biggest islands.
Vidi Livu and Vanualavu.
Many people live near the sea.
The country is peaceful and full of nature.
What language do people speak in Fiji?
People in Fiji speak Fijian, Hindi and English.
These are the three official languages.
English is used in schools and government.
Many people are bilingual or trilingual.
Fijian is the local language.
Hindi is spoken by people with Indian roots.
What is the weather like in Fiji?
Fiji has tropical weather.
It is warm and humid all year.
There are two seasons, the wet season and the dry season.
The wet season is from November to April.
It can rain a lot, but it is still warm.
The dry season is from May to October.
It is sunny and cooler.
Fiji is a great place to enjoy the sun and sea.
What does Fiji look like?
Fiji has beaches, mountains, forests and volcanoes.
The water is blue and clear.
There are many coral reefs near the islands.
The land is green and full of coconut trees,
flowers and tropical plants.
Some islands are small and quiet.
Others have hotels, towns and activities.
What animals live in Fiji?
Fiji has many birds, lizards and sea animals.
You can see parrots, fruit, bats and geckos.
In the ocean, you can see fish, sea turtles and coral.
People go snorkeling and diving to explore the sea.
Fiji has many protected areas to help animals and nature.
What do people eat in Fiji?
Fiji and food is fresh and healthy.
People eat fish, rice, taro, cassava and vegetables.
Coconut is used in many dishes.
One traditional food is called lovo.
Lovo is meat, fish and vegetables cooked underground with hot stones.
People also eat Indian style curries and roti because of the Indian community.
For dessert, they enjoy tropical fruits like pineapple,
papaya and banana.
What is life like in Fiji?
Life in Fiji is relaxed and friendly.
People smile and say hello.
The Fiji ingredient is bula.
It means hello and life.
Would you like to try?
Say, bula.
Families are important.
People help each other.
Villages are strong communities.
Music and dance are part of life.
People sing songs and play the guitar and drums.
Traditional dances are colorful and fun.
Some fun facts about Fiji.
Fiji became independent in 1970.
The flag is light blue with the union jack and a shield.
The money is called the Fiji and Dollar.
Rugby is the most popular sport.
Fiji's rugby team is one of the best in the world.
Fiji is one of the happiest countries in the Pacific.
Now you know many things about Fiji.
You know where it is, what people speak and what the weather is like.
You learned about the islands, the sea, the food and the people.
Great work.
I am Emili.
Goodbye.
Or as they say in Fiji.
Mo say.
